# Overview

Per-sample quality of the alignments and of the sample identity, read from
the workflow's QC outputs. A call in a sample that fails here is reviewed for
a technical cause first: low or uneven coverage, contamination, a library
with many duplicates, or a sample swap. Every sample of the run is shown,
including those left out of the CH report (marked as excluded).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(yaml)

# Rendered by the qc_report step of the workflow (workflow/scripts/render_report.R),
# with the project folder holding qc/, contamination/ and logs/.
PROJECT_DIR <- params$project_dir
RESULTS_DIR <- params$results_dir

if (!nzchar(PROJECT_DIR) || !dir.exists(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "qc"))) {
  stop("Set project_dir to the project folder holding qc/: ", PROJECT_DIR)
}

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = PROJECT_DIR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r inputs}
n_report <- function(df, label) {
  message(sprintf("%-40s n = %d", label, nrow(df)))
  df
}

# Most recent real run (not a dry run) whose settings carry a qc block
settings_files <- sort(list.files("logs/batches", pattern = "^run_.*_settings\\.yaml$",
                                  full.names = TRUE))
settings_list <- lapply(settings_files, yaml::read_yaml)
usable <- vapply(settings_list,
                 function(s) !is.null(s$qc) && !isTRUE(s$run$dry_run),
                 logical(1))
if (!any(usable)) stop("No run settings with a qc block in logs/batches/")
settings <- settings_list[[max(which(usable))]]

wgs <- identical(settings$data_type, "wgs")
thr <- if (wgs) settings$qc$thresholds_wgs else settings$qc$thresholds
min_dp <- settings$ch_filter$min_dp

flags <- read.delim("qc/qc_flags.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
                    na.strings = c("NA", "")) %>%
  n_report("samples in qc_flags.tsv")

# Coverage columns differ between exome and genome metrics
coverage_col <- if (wgs) "mean_coverage" else "mean_target_coverage"
breadth_col  <- if (wgs) "pct_20x" else "pct_target_20x"
coverage_min <- thr$min_mean_coverage
breadth_min  <- if (wgs) thr$min_pct_20x else thr$min_pct_target_20x

# Samples left out of the reports (report.exclude_samples): marked, not removed
excluded <- character(0)
if (nzchar(params$exclude_samples)) {
  ids <- trimws(sub("#.*$", "", readLines(params$exclude_samples, warn = FALSE)))
  excluded <- unique(ids[nzchar(ids)])
}
flags$excluded <- flags$sample %in% excluded

# Contamination estimate per sample (GATK CalculateContamination)
contamination <- do.call(rbind, lapply(flags$sample, function(s) {
  path <- file.path("contamination", paste0(s, ".contamination.table"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Contamination table not found: ", path)
  table <- read.delim(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  data.frame(sample = s, contamination = table$contamination[1], contamination_error = table$error[1])
})) %>% n_report("contamination tables")

# Input type per sample, from the sample sheet of the run
sheet <- read.delim(settings$samples, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
if (!"bam" %in% names(sheet)) sheet$bam <- ""
input <- sheet %>%
  dplyr::mutate(input = dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("\\.cram$", bam) ~ "CRAM",
    grepl("\\.bam$", bam)  ~ "BAM",
    TRUE                   ~ "FASTQ")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(sample) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(input = paste(sort(unique(input)), collapse = "+"), units = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups = "drop")

qc <- flags %>%
  dplyr::left_join(contamination, by = "sample") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(input, by = "sample")

missing_input <- qc$sample[is.na(qc$input)]
if (length(missing_input) > 0) {
  stop("Samples in qc_flags.tsv but not in the sample sheet ", settings$samples, ": ",
       paste(missing_input, collapse = ", "))
}

# One point per sample, ordered by value; names shown for small cohorts only
sample_plot <- function(df, column, x_label, lines = NULL) {
  df <- df[!is.na(df[[column]]), , drop = FALSE]
  df$sample <- factor(df$sample, levels = df$sample[order(df[[column]])])
  plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[column]], y = sample, colour = status, shape = excluded)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(PASS = "#2171B5", FLAG = "#B2182B")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 4), labels = c("FALSE" = "included", "TRUE" = "excluded")) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL)
  for (line in lines) plot <- plot + geom_vline(xintercept = line$x, linetype = line$type)
  if (nrow(df) > 60) plot <- plot + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  plot
}
plot_height <- min(12, max(3, nrow(qc) * 0.15))
```

## Summary

```{r summary}
data.frame(
  samples       = nrow(qc),
  PASS          = sum(qc$status == "PASS"),
  FLAG          = sum(qc$status == "FLAG"),
  excluded      = sum(qc$excluded),
  data_type     = if (wgs) "WGS" else "WES"
)

flag_counts <- qc %>%
  dplyr::filter(flags != "-") %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(flags, sep = ";") %>%
  dplyr::count(flags, name = "samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(samples))
if (nrow(flag_counts) == 0) message("No sample is flagged.")
flag_counts

qc %>%
  dplyr::filter(status == "FLAG" | excluded) %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, flags, excluded, dplyr::all_of(c(coverage_col, breadth_col)), contamination)
```

## Input

```{r input}
qc %>% dplyr::count(input, units, name = "samples")
```

# Coverage

Calls need a depth of at least `r min_dp` (`ch_filter.min_dp`) at their
position. A sample whose mean coverage is near or below that depth has little
of the panel callable, so its negative status says little. The dashed line
marks `ch_filter.min_dp`, the dotted line the QC coverage threshold
(`r coverage_min`).

```{r coverage, fig.width=8, fig.height=plot_height}
sample_plot(qc, coverage_col, if (wgs) "Mean coverage" else "Mean target coverage",
            list(list(x = min_dp, type = "dashed"), list(x = coverage_min, type = "dotted")))
```

Fraction of the `r if (wgs) "calling regions" else "capture targets"` covered
at 20x or more; the dotted line is the QC threshold (`r breadth_min`).

```{r breadth, fig.width=8, fig.height=plot_height}
sample_plot(qc, breadth_col, "Fraction at 20x or more", list(list(x = breadth_min, type = "dotted")))
```

# Library

Fraction of bases excluded from coverage as duplicates, the value the QC
flag uses (dotted line: `r thr$max_pct_dupe`); a high fraction means fewer
independent molecules than the depth suggests. The duplicate rate of all reads
from MarkDuplicates is in the exported table (`pct_dup_markdup`).

```{r duplication, fig.width=8, fig.height=plot_height}
sample_plot(qc, "pct_exc_dupe", "Duplicate fraction excluded from coverage",
            list(list(x = thr$max_pct_dupe, type = "dotted")))
```

Median insert size: an outlier can point to degraded DNA or a different
library protocol.

```{r insert_size, fig.width=8, fig.height=plot_height}
sample_plot(qc, "median_insert_size", "Median insert size (bp)")
```

# Contamination

Fraction of reads from another individual, estimated by CalculateContamination
at common variant sites and passed to FilterMutectCalls. Contamination adds
low-VAF calls that look like small clones, so calls in a contaminated sample
are reviewed before they are read as CH. The workflow sets no threshold here.

```{r contamination, fig.width=8, fig.height=plot_height}
sample_plot(qc, "contamination", "Estimated contamination")
qc %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, contamination, contamination_error) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(contamination)) %>%
  head(10)
```

# Sex and identity

Mean depth on chromosomes X and Y at the somalier sites, relative to the
autosomes. Male and female samples form two clusters on the Y ratio.
`r if (is.null(settings$qc$sex_y_ratio_male)) "No sex is inferred until qc.sex_y_ratio_male is set: choose a value between the two clusters below." else paste0("Samples with a Y ratio of at least ", settings$qc$sex_y_ratio_male, " (qc.sex_y_ratio_male, dashed line) are called male.")`

```{r sex, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
sex_plot <- ggplot(qc, aes(x = x_depth_ratio, y = y_depth_ratio, colour = inferred_sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "X / autosome depth", y = "Y / autosome depth", colour = "inferred sex")
if (!is.null(settings$qc$sex_y_ratio_male)) {
  sex_plot <- sex_plot + geom_hline(yintercept = settings$qc$sex_y_ratio_male, linetype = "dashed")
}
sex_plot
qc %>% dplyr::filter(grepl("SEX_MISMATCH", flags)) %>% dplyr::select(sample, inferred_sex, y_depth_ratio)
```

Relatedness between every pair of samples. Unrelated individuals sit near 0,
first-degree relatives near 0.5, and two samples from the same individual
near 1: a duplicate or a sample swap. Pairs at or above
`r settings$qc$min_relatedness_list` (`qc.min_relatedness_list`) are listed;
pairs at or above `r settings$qc$min_relatedness_flag` are flagged
POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE.

```{r relatedness, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
pairs <- read.delim("qc/somalier/relate.pairs.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
names(pairs) <- sub("^#", "", names(pairs))
pairs <- n_report(pairs, "sample pairs")
if (nrow(pairs) == 0) {
  message("A single sample: no pairs.")
} else {
  print(
    ggplot(pairs, aes(x = relatedness)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey60") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = settings$qc$min_relatedness_list, linetype = "dotted") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = settings$qc$min_relatedness_flag, linetype = "dashed") +
      theme_classic() +
      labs(x = "Relatedness", y = "Sample pairs")
  )
}
related <- pairs %>%
  dplyr::filter(relatedness >= settings$qc$min_relatedness_list) %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_a, sample_b, relatedness, dplyr::any_of(c("ibs0", "ibs2", "n"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(relatedness))
if (nrow(related) == 0) message("No pair at or above ", settings$qc$min_relatedness_list, ".")
related
```

# Export

```{r export}
dir.create(RESULTS_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(qc,      file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "qc_summary.csv"),        row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(related, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "qc_related_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
